## Findings
- claim-1: For \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\), \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and this submodule is an ideal. [source-2@L1310-L1321|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The map \(s_\lambda\mapsto s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\) induces \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}/\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^W_+\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}\), and the surviving Schur classes are indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2@L1321-L1331|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Writing \(q=n-r\), the excerpt yields \[ I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,\qquad \Lambda/I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda. \] The second equality follows by quotienting the Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis by the coordinate submodule defining \(I_{r,q}\).
## Strategy
The requested target is established by validated claims `claim-1` and `claim-2`: source-2 defines \(I_{r,q}\) as the Schur span outside \(q^r\), proves it is an ideal, and identifies the surviving quotient Schur basis. Claim `claim-3` records the immediate basiswise reformulation.
